source: CAMFAD student thesis: "Establishment of a New Coconut Plantation Farm", National School of Agriculture, July 1994
text:
The thesis closes by arguing that Cambodia had not yet developed any single crop production line to its full potential on a wide scale at the time of writing (1994), including crops tied to the country's climate and land resources, and that applying agricultural science more systematically could modernize the sector, raise national income, and make Cambodian agricultural production more competitive regionally.

Coconut planting is presented as a strong candidate for this kind of development -- a crop that could become a meaningful national income generator if plantations are properly planned and managed. The authors frame their cost/revenue analysis (projecting roughly USD 56.7 million in net profit over 10 years at a 10,000-hectare development scale) as an illustrative starting point rather than a guaranteed outcome, explicitly noting that year-to-year results depend on management quality, and that coconut's long productive lifespan (25-30 years) leaves room for yield and price to improve over time. The thesis is offered as a small contribution intended to help guide further study and interest in coconut plantation development in Cambodia.
